clue.text: Liberty of unrestricted religious title

parts.note: something unrestricted is free
Dom is a title given to some monks, Benedictines among them

explanation.surface: A churchman's honorific comes with no strings attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberty and its synonym both mean the state of being free from control.

clue.text: Just, unknown country this imaginary realm

parts.note: just means fair
Y is an algebraic unknown
a country is a land

explanation.surface: A fair, mysterious country is a dream kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The magical realm of the little people, a place of make-believe.

clue.text: The farthest objective to the majority

parts.note: an end is a goal or objective
most means the greater part, the majority

explanation.surface: The most remote aim belongs to the greater number.
explanation.definitionFit: Situated at the very end, the most distant point.

clue.text: Lydia met Richard in part of the Circle line

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Two people met on a stretch of London's Circle Line underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route; here it is a geometric line through a circle's centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A diameter is the line across a circle through its centre, so diametric describes it.

clue.text: The goddess's dwelling place, according to hearsay

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: according to hearsay says the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a mews is a row of stables converted into homes

explanation.surface: Rumour reveals where a goddess lives.
explanation.walkthrough: A mews is a British street of former stables turned into houses.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the nine daughters of Zeus who inspire the arts.

clue.text: Disarming not always successful it seems

explanation.surface: Someone who lays down arms seems to have a patchy record.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the answer as two words, as in the saying 'you win some, you lose some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Disarming charm is engaging and attractive; read as two words, the answer describes someone who wins only some of the time.

clue.text: Dishonest undertaking is in breach of the law

parts.note: dishonest dealing is wrong
an undertaking is a doing, an act

explanation.surface: Cheating on a promise counts as breaking the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal or immoral behaviour, an offence.

clue.text: Rustic swain turns up as this gypsy

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Damon is the stock name of a shepherd lover in pastoral poetry

explanation.surface: A country lad reveals himself as a traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: Damon is a conventional name for a shepherd in pastoral verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home, a traveller.

clue.text: This woodland growth is no freak mutation

indicators.note: a mutation changes things, so the letters of these words are altered in order

explanation.surface: A plant in the woods that is quite normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mutation' scrambles NO FREAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate fern found growing in woods.

clue.text: Gains interest when listeners absorb the point

indicators.note: to absorb something is to take it inside, so the point goes within

parts.note: ears are what we listen with
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The audience becomes engaged when they take in a key point.
explanation.walkthrough: N is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Money in an account collects interest, so it earns.

clue.text: Country needing men for shipping

parts.note: add the word men to the name of the country and you get the old trading vessels that sailed to and from it for the East ... Company

explanation.surface: A nation short of sailors for its merchant fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: An Indiaman was a large merchant ship trading with the subcontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: The country plus 'men' names a class of ship, so the clue identifies the nation through its ships.

clue.text: So he is a snob

parts.note: snob is an old dialect word for a cobbler, so the clue describes a mender of footwear, not a social climber

explanation.surface: A remark labelling someone a social climber.
explanation.walkthrough: Snob's original sense, still in dictionaries, is a cobbler; 'So he' also lurks at the start of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler, the old meaning of snob, is someone who makes and mends footwear.

clue.text: Old soldiers like Sergeant Meryll

explanation.surface: Veterans resembling a sergeant from an operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: Sergeant Meryll is a Yeoman of the Guard in Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta of that name; the Yeoman Warders of the Tower of London are retired soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeoman Warders are ex-servicemen, and Gilbert and Sullivan's Sergeant Meryll is one of their guard.

clue.text: Old promontory of antiquity

parts.note: old means aged
ness is a headland, familiar from Scottish place names such as Loch Ness's neighbours

explanation.surface: An ancient headland from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiquity here means great age, the condition of being very old.

clue.text: Made merry like the Duke of Plaza Toro

definitions.text: like the Duke of Plaza Toro

explanation.surface: Partied like a comic duke.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's The Gondoliers the Duke of Plaza-Toro is 'that celebrated, cultivated, underrated nobleman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked an occasion with festivities, and famous, as the duke's song describes him.

clue.text: Focal point of union meeting

parts.note: the union is a marriage and the meeting a wedding, whose centre is where the couple stand in church

explanation.surface: The centre of attention at a trade union gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union meeting' suggests trade unions; it is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A church wedding centres on the communion table where the couple make their vows.

clue.text: Queen Cleo moved by such oratory

indicators.note: moved says the letters of the two words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Cleopatra is stirred by fine speech-making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' looks emotional but shuffles QUEEN CLEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent, persuasive speaking is the quality that fine oratory displays.

clue.text: Cinema director working in the dark

definitions.text: Cinema director working in the dark

parts.words: Cinema director working in the dark
parts.note: not a film director but someone who directs patrons to their seats with a torch while the lights are down

explanation.surface: A film-maker shooting in poor light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director' suggests a film-maker; it is someone who shows people to their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who guides filmgoers to their places in the darkened auditorium.

clue.text: Premise, he formulated for astronomical data

indicators.note: formulated means put together afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man devises a theory for star charts.
explanation.definitionFit: A table giving the positions of heavenly bodies on successive dates.

clue.text: Fearful position a model can bend into

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing a perilous position, like that of the courtier under the hanging sword

indicators.note: bend into says the letters of these words are twisted into a new shape

explanation.surface: A frightening pose that a fashion model can contort herself into.
explanation.walkthrough: Damocles sat beneath a sword hung by a single hair, so a Damoclean position is one of constant peril.
explanation.definitionFit: The courtier Damocles feasted under a sword suspended by one hair, a byword for impending danger.

clue.text: The Tower, a money-maker, will accept a note

indicators.note: will accept means takes in, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: the mint makes coins
re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The Tower of London, home of the Royal Mint, takes a banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the Tower of London, which once housed the Royal Mint.
explanation.definitionFit: The slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is given.

clue.text: Couple in hold-up

explanation.surface: Pairing up during a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple a trailer is to attach it, and a delay or snag is a problem of that name.

clue.text: Tangible cat up on part of the roof

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tile is one piece of a roof covering

explanation.surface: A real cat climbs onto the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to be touched or felt.

clue.text: Help. to haul — by pulling or pushing it?

parts.note: to give a hand is to help
to cart something is to haul it

explanation.surface: Help is needed to drag something along, whether you pull or push.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes how the small barrow is moved.
explanation.definitionFit: A small barrow is moved by hand, either pulled or pushed along.

clue.text: Tries to dispose of birds

explanation.surface: Attempts to get rid of some birds.
explanation.definitionFit: To peddle goods is to try to sell them, and the birds of prey share the name.

clue.text: Large piece of toast for food

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter lost

parts.note: cheers is said as a toast

explanation.surface: A big slice of toast to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large piece of' drops the last letter of CHEERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Good cheer means food and drink, fare.

clue.text: Weight of old penny charm perhaps

parts.note: D was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British money

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word charm is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: An old coin may be a lucky trinket.
explanation.walkthrough: The D for a penny comes from the Latin denarius, used in Britain before decimal currency in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: An old unit of apothecaries' weight, an eighth of an ounce.

clue.text: Possibly a catch in this conveyance

explanation.surface: There may be a snag with this vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare is a catching device, and a light horse-drawn carriage is also called this.

clue.text: Seventeenth century battle in China?

explanation.surface: A civil-war battle fought in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromwell won the Battle of Worcester in 1651; the city also gives its name to a famous porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1651 battle ended the English Civil War, and the English city's factory made a well-known porcelain.

clue.text: Judge describing Bruce's spider

explanation.surface: A judge talking about a famous Scottish spider.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says Robert the Bruce, king of Scots, watched a spider try again and again to spin its web, and took heart.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tries cases is a judge, and the persevering spider kept on making attempts.

clue.text: Joined river in dust storm

indicators.note: in puts the river inside the stormed letters
a storm whirls the letters of the word dust about

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A river merged during a dust storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' looks like part of the dust storm picture but signals the anagram; the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitched together, as a surgeon closes a wound with stitches.

clue.text: The noble lady is a mole, they say

indicators.note: they say tells us the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a mole is a breakwater or pier, and 'is' is kept as it stands after it

explanation.surface: A titled woman is called a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' suggests a spy or the animal; it is a pier. PIER IS spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman holding a title in her own right or as a lord's wife.
